title: the held-instance proof measures the Python launcher on every OS and reads UNRAN where tmux is absent
intention: test_a_launch_moves_off_a_held_instance.py drives cairn/devices/cc/superclaude.py through sys.executable, stages its holds as live python children, and its tmux tooth reads UNRAN where tmux is absent.
why: Measured 2026-11-23: the proof drove the bash launcher, which Windows cannot run, so 4 of 5 teeth failed while the Python launcher moved off a held instance correctly.
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8 (a proof must measure the code, not the host); outline 9.4.8.1 (a tooth this host cannot run reads not-run); outline 10.3.2.1 (superclaude is Python on every box)
how: run the Python launcher via sys.executable; stage live and dead pids as sys.executable children; compare the flags home by Path; raise 'UNRAN: ...' in the tmux tooth when tmux is absent; end the proof with run_teeth so the reason prints.

clauses.claim: a live loop.pid at instance 0 moves a dry run to launching 1
a dead pid at instance 0 does not hold it
two held instances move a dry run to the third
a held word name keeps its name with an _N suffix
a tmux session cairn_cc_<n> holds like a loop, or the tooth's FAIL line says UNRAN where tmux is absent

decisions.text: D1: run the Python launcher via sys.executable; stage live and dead pids as sys.executable children; compare the flags home by Path; raise 'UNRAN: ...' in the tmux tooth when tmux is absent; end the proof with run_teeth so the reason prints.

out: cairn/devices/cc/superclaude (the bash launcher, retired by c3cd232ba0cf's last child)

measured.saw: On Windows 4 of 5 teeth failed driving the bash launcher; the Python launcher printed 'launching 1' beside a live pid; tmux tooth 5 has no tmux to stage with.
measured.how: ran the proof natively on akiendell (Windows) and read printed stdout; akiendelllinux ran branch akiendell/ab-proofs at e8deae9d0 under bin/cairn test --exec: all teeth ok
